rationale: Without a code signing configuration, Lambda accepts any deployment package presented by a principal holding lambda:UpdateFunctionCode, and the new code runs on the next invocation with the function's execution role. Nothing ties the archive that runs to the pipeline that was supposed to produce it, so a stolen deployment credential, a compromised build step or an object written directly into the S3 bucket the function is deployed from all reach production the same way a legitimate release does. Code signing makes Lambda check, at deployment time, that the archive was signed by a signing profile the account trusts, and that it was not modified since.
remediation: Create a Signer signing profile for the function, publish deployment packages through it, and attach a code signing configuration to the function with UntrustedArtifactOnDeployment set to Enforce
